name: MonarchThemeToggle
title: ThemeToggle
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow with SegmentedButton; androidx.compose.material3.DropdownMenu with DropdownMenuItem and RadioButton for the menu variant
summary: Light, dark or system theme: a segmented control or a menu button that reports the MonarchScheme the app passes to MonarchTheme.
whenToUse: In a settings screen (segmented) or in a toolbar or account menu (menu) when people may choose the appearance of the app instead of following the system.
whenNotToUse: For any other choice between two to five options use SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow directly (segmented-control). Do not add it when the app always follows the system setting.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchThemeToggle(scheme: MonarchScheme, onSchemeChange: (MonarchScheme) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, variant: MonarchThemeToggleVariant = MonarchThemeToggleVariant.Segmented, size: MonarchThemeToggleSize = MonarchThemeToggleSize.Md, enabled: Boolean = true, showLabel: Boolean = true, icon: (@Composable (MonarchScheme) -> Unit)? = null, labels: MonarchThemeToggleLabels = MonarchThemeToggleLabels())
public enum class MonarchThemeToggleVariant { Segmented, Menu }
public enum class MonarchThemeToggleSize { Sm, Md }
public class MonarchThemeToggleLabels(title: String? = null, light: String? = null, dark: String? = null, system: String? = null)
public object MonarchThemeToggleStorage { public fun storageValue(scheme: MonarchScheme): String; public fun scheme(value: String?): MonarchScheme? }

options.name: scheme
options.description: The current choice: Light, Dark or System. The app keeps it and passes it to MonarchTheme(scheme = …).

options.name: onSchemeChange
options.description: Called with the choice the user picks. Not called when the current choice is picked again.

options.name: variant
options.description: Segmented shows three segments; Menu shows one ghost button that opens the three choices.

options.name: size
options.description: Segmented: the caption or the label type for the names. Menu: the Sm or Md Monarch button.

options.name: enabled
options.description: Whether the user can change the choice.

options.name: showLabel
options.description: Menu only: whether the button shows the current choice's name beside the icon. The name is always spoken, and shown when there is no icon.

options.name: icon
options.description: An icon for a choice (sun, moon, half-filled circle) on the menu button and in the menu. Decorative; Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings Theme, Light, Dark and System.

states.name: light, dark, system
states.description: The selected segment with the Material check mark, or the menu button's name and the checked radio item in the menu.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A Material 3 dropdown menu with the title Theme and three radio items; picking one closes it.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The segments or the menu button use the disabled colors and do not respond.

appearance: The segmented variant is the Material segmented button row with the Monarch color mapping: the selected segment takes the secondary container color mapped from the accent subtle role, the border is the default border role. The menu button is the ghost Monarch button; the menu is the Material menu on the raised surface. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles.
platformNotes: The web toggle reads and writes the shared rook_theme cookie and applies the theme to the html element. In an Android app there is no shared cookie: the toggle only reports the choice; the app stores it (DataStore or SharedPreferences) and passes it to MonarchTheme(scheme = …). MonarchThemeToggleStorage gives the same light, dark and system values as the cookie and the iOS storageValue(for:). The web's controlled and uncontrolled forms become one hoisted value, as Compose state is. The web menu variant's side and align options are not offered: the Material dropdown menu places itself. The web draws sun, moon and system glyphs; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the icon slot is empty by default and the names are always shown in the segments. Same names and vocabulary as iOS, with scheme and onSchemeChange instead of a binding.
accessibility: The segment row is named Theme; each segment is a radio button with its name, and the current one is selected.
The menu button is named Theme and its state is the current choice's name, also when only the icon is shown.
The menu has a Theme heading and three radio items, the current one selected and marked with a filled radio button, not color alone.
Each segment and the menu button have a 48dp touch target; the segments follow the reading order in right-to-left layouts.
The names stay whole at font scale 2.0.
edgeCases: Picking the current choice again does not call onSchemeChange.
MonarchThemeToggleStorage.scheme returns null for a missing or unknown stored value; use the app's default then.
System follows the system dark theme setting while the app runs, because MonarchTheme reads isSystemInDarkTheme.
In the menu variant with showLabel false and no icon, the name is shown anyway so the button is never empty.

examples.title: Appearance setting
A menu in a toolbar, stored as text
examples.setup:
var stored by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>("dark") }
val scheme = MonarchThemeToggleStorage.scheme(stored) ?: MonarchScheme.System
examples.code:
MonarchThemeToggle(
    scheme = scheme,
    onSchemeChange = { stored = MonarchThemeToggleStorage.storageValue(it) },
    variant = MonarchThemeToggleVariant.Menu,
    size = MonarchThemeToggleSize.Sm,
)
